data.title: Flipper Zero dark web firmware bypasses rolling code security
data.author: lq9AJ8yrfs
data.article_summary: YouTube频道Talking Sasquach最近测试了一种Flipper Zero的自定义固件，可以破解现代车辆使用的滚码安全系统。与传统的RollJam攻击需要干扰信号并重放不同，这种新攻击只需捕获一次遥控钥匙信号，无需干扰，即可完全模拟钥匙的所有功能，如开锁、关锁和开启后备箱。这种攻击通过逆向工程滚码序列或利用所谓的"RollBack"攻击实现，使原钥匙失效。受影响车辆包括克莱斯勒、道奇、菲亚特、福特、现代、Jeep、起亚、三菱和斯巴鲁等。目前尚无简单修复方法，可能需要大规模召回车辆。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：无钥匙进入系统和汽车钥匙扣的安全性及潜在漏洞

不同观点：
• [kj4ips] 认为许多滚码系统基于KeyLoq技术，该技术设计良好，但存在一个致命弱点：如果掌握了"制造商密钥"，通过两次捕捉信号即可破解序列密钥。虽然直接暴力破解成本高，但获取制造商密钥并不困难。
• [RachelF] 指出无钥匙启动系统存在安全隐患，认为多重安全机制更为可靠。同时提到汽车制造商可能从车辆被盗中获益，因为保险赔付常促使顾客购买新车。
• [rootsudo] 质疑为何将相关技术与"暗网"过度关联，认为使用这些技术本身不一定违法，尽管在美国可能涉及法律问题（如USC 18 1029/30）。
• [Terr_] 提出如果信号不是广播传输，而是通过物理接触或人耳可感知的声波传输，可能提高安全性。认为锁车操作相对解锁操作更安全。
• [finaard] 认为某些视频内容缺乏实质性信息，只是重新包装了已有的滚码漏洞。
• [palata] 关心钥匙扣失效后的后果，询问用户是否能自行重置，还是必须由零售商处理。
• [tzs] 询问如果不按钥匙扣按钮是否能避免被攻击，并提到自己的车在靠近车门时可通过按车门把手上的按钮解锁。
• [theoreticalmal] 认为攻击的主要威胁不是车辆被盗，而是攻击者通过捕获按键信号使原钥匙失效，迫使用户重新编程，从而造成不便。
• [beagle3] 提到自己的保险公司要求安装代码输入设备以防止汽车被盗，认为尽管初期麻烦，但能有效防止常见盗车手段。
• [piyuv] 担心政客可能因无钥匙系统的不安全性而禁止相关工具（如Flipper Zero），而不是正视问题本身。
• [antirez] 猜测攻击针对的是KEELOQ协议，并质疑芯片中的加密技术是否真的被完全破解，表示需要进一步了解攻击细节。
• [move-on-by] 询问为何某些汽车制造商（如Chevrolet、Toyota）未受影响，而其他制造商（如Ford、Hyundai）则存在漏洞，是否有未被测试或使用不同技术的原因。
• [geekamongus] 提到在亚马逊上可以轻松购买福特车队的钥匙，从而解锁大多数福特卡车和面包车，质疑当前系统的安全性。
• [joelthelion] 质疑为何汽车不使用公钥加密技术，是成本问题还是其他原因。
• [IshKebab] 对漏洞的有效性表示震惊，认为实现该系统的工程师应该知道其不安全性，并表示自己不会想到去检查这种漏洞。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于无钥匙系统的安全性以及如何有效防止攻击。
• 不同评论者对制造商密钥的泄露途径、攻击的可行性及后果、以及潜在解决方案（如公钥加密、物理接触信号传输）进行了讨论。
• 对汽车制造商是否从车辆被盗中获益的质疑，以及对政客可能禁止相关工具的担忧也被提出。

44830408.article_content:
Over on YouTube Talking Sasquach has recently tested custom firmware for the Flipper Zero that can entirely break the rolling code security system used on most modern vehicles. Rolling code security works by using a synchronized algorithm between a transmitter and receiver to generate a new, unique code for each transmission, preventing replay attacks and unauthorized access.
In the past we've discussed an attack against rolling code security systems called
RollJam
, which works by jamming the original keyfob signal so the vehicle cannot receive it, and at the same time recording it for later use. However, this attack is difficult to perform in reality.
For this new attack to work, all that is needed is a single button-press capture from the keyfob, without any jamming. Just from that single capture, it is able to emulate all the keyfob's functions, including lock, unlock, and unlock trunk. A consequence of this is that the original keyfob gets out of sync, and will no longer function.
According to the Talking Sasquatch, the attack works by simply reverse engineering the rolling code sequence, either through sequence leaks or prior brute forcing of the sequence from a large list of known codes. However,
another article
mentions that the firmware is based on the "
RollBack
" attack, which works by playing back captured rolling codes in a specific order to initiate a 'rollback' of the synchronization system.
Regardless of the method, videos demonstrating the attack show that only a single capture is needed to emulate a keyfob completely.
Affected vehicles include Chrysler, Dodge, Fiat, Ford, Hyundai, Jeep, Kia, Mitsubishi and Subaru. As of yet, there appears to be no easy fix for this, other than mass vehicle recalls.

data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了"Ranking Playground"实验，特别是"4o vs 5"的对比测试。参与者在不知模型具体身份的情况下，对GPT-4o和GPT-5的回答进行盲选A/B对比，并投票选择更喜欢的答案。实验结束后，参与者可以查看自己更频繁选择的模型。该实验旨在通过用户反馈比较不同GPT版本的性能和用户偏好。用户还可以通过"Explore"功能从五个匿名模型中每轮挑选两个最佳答案，最终了解自己最常选择的模型。

data.title: Buttercup is now open-source
data.author: wglb
data.article_summary: Trail of Bits宣布在DARPA的AI Cyber Challenge（AIxCC）中获得第二名，并将其开发的网络推理系统Buttercup开源。Buttercup是一个全自动、AI驱动的系统，旨在发现和修补开源软件中的漏洞。它包括四个主要组件： orchestration/UI、vulnerability discovery（使用AI增强的模糊测试发现漏洞）、contextual analysis（利用静态分析工具建立程序模型）和patch generation（多代理系统生成和验证补丁）。为了便于使用，他们提供了一个可以在普通笔记本电脑上运行的独立版本，并支持x86-64 Linux系统，部分支持ARM64系统如MacOS设备。运行Buttercup需要至少8核CPU、16GB RAM、100GB空闲磁盘空间和网络连接，以及第三方大型语言模型（如OpenAI或Anthropic）的API密钥。用户可以通过克隆代码库并运行简单命令来设置和使用Buttercup。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

44841285.article_content:
Page content
We’re thrilled to announce that Trail of Bits won second place in DARPA’s AI Cyber Challenge (AIxCC)! Now that the competition has ended, we can finally make Buttercup, our CRS (Cyber Reasoning System), open source. We’re thrilled to make Buttercup broadly available and see how the security community uses, extends, and benefits from it.
To ensure as many people as possible can use Buttercup, we created a standalone version that runs on a typical laptop. We’ve also tuned this version to work within an AI budget appropriate for individual projects rather than a massive competition at scale. In addition to releasing the standalone version of Buttercup, we’re also open-sourcing the versions that competed in AIxCC’s semifinal and final rounds.
In the rest of this post, we’ll provide a high-level overview of how Buttercup works, how to get started using it, and what’s in store for it next. If you’d prefer to go straight to the code, check it out
here on GitHub
.
How Buttercup works
Buttercup is a fully automated, AI-driven system for discovering and patching vulnerabilities in open-source software. Buttercup has four main components:
Orchestration/UI
coordinates the overall actions of Buttercup’s other components and displays information about vulnerabilities discovered and patches generated by the system. In addition to a typical web interface, Buttercup also reports its logs and system events to a SigNoz telemetry server to make it easy for users to see what Buttercup is doing.
Vulnerability discovery
uses AI-augmented mutational fuzzing to find program inputs that demonstrate vulnerabilities in the program. Buttercup’s vulnerability discovery engine is based on
OSS-Fuzz
/
Clusterfuzz
and uses
libFuzzer
and
Jazzer
to find vulnerabilities.
Contextual analysis
uses traditional static analysis tools to create queryable program models that are used to provide context to AI models used in vulnerability discovery and patching. Buttercup uses
tree-sitter
and
CodeQuery
to build the program model.
Patch generation
is a multi-agentic system for creating and validating software patches for vulnerabilities discovered by Buttercup. Buttercup’s patch generation system uses seven distinct AI agents to create robust patches that fix vulnerabilities it finds and avoid breaking the program’s other functionality.
The following flowchart depicts how these components help Buttercup discover and patch vulnerabilities:
Figure 1: Conceptual overview of Buttercup’s vulnerability discovery and patching pipeline
When Buttercup is started, it waits for tasking from the user in the form of an OSS-Fuzz-compatible source code repository. Once tasked, Buttercup retrieves the code repository, builds the program with and without various sanitizers enabled, and begins fuzzing the program with the help of an AI-based input generator. When inputs trigger sanitizers, timeouts, or crashes in the program, these inputs are recorded as proofs of vulnerability (PoVs).
Next, Buttercup’s orchestrator deduplicates PoVs and sends unique crashes to the patch generation system for patching. The patch generation system, using information from the contextual analysis system, iteratively creates, tests, and refines patches until it generates a patch that 1) prevents the PoV and its duplicates from triggering the vulnerability and 2) maintains the program’s other functions. Finally, Buttercup’s orchestrator retains the PoVs and patches so they can be reported to the user.
Getting started
We’ve made it easy for individual users to get Buttercup up and running on a typical laptop. Buttercup works best on x86-64 Linux systems, but does partially support ARM64 systems like MacOS devices. You’ll need at least 8 CPU cores, 16 GB of RAM, 100GB of free disk space, and an active network connection to run Buttercup. You’ll also need to provide an API key for at least one third-party LLM provider like OpenAI or Anthropic. Don’t worry: we make it easy to set a cost limit so Buttercup doesn’t run up an unexpectedly large bill.
All you need to do is clone
Buttercup’s code repository
, ensure that you have a few common system packages installed, and run a few easy commands in your terminal:
Setup:
Guides the user through installing Buttercup on the system and configuring it with AI API keys.
Deploy:
Creates a fully localized cluster with all of Buttercup’s components running within pods. Here’s what it looks like when Buttercup is started and ready to process a new task:
Figure 2: Buttercup ready to find and patch vulnerabilities
Send task
: Sends Buttercup a sample code repository with an intentionally inserted vulnerability to demonstrate Buttercup’s capabilities. It takes Buttercup less than 10 minutes to find and patch the vulnerability.
Open UI
: Start up Buttercup’s browser-based UI to see the PoVs and patches that Buttercup has discovered. Here’s what the Buttercup web UI looks like when it finds vulnerabilities and patches them:
Figure 3: Buttercup web UI a

Once an empire existed on which the sun did not set for over two centuries. Soon
the sun will set
because that country is
paying £18bn
to give away its last naval base in the Indian Ocean. What happened?
Britain’s slide from global hegemony to irrelevance wasn’t because it once had the world in GDP per capita, but is now
doing
famously
badly
relative to other developed countries. Income gaps among rich nations are modest, and weaker economies like the USSR (never above 43 % of US GDP per capita) still packed strategic punch.
1
What shrank Britain’s weight was not low fertility either—its birth rates stayed high, at least until WW1—but mass emigration. The people, and the children they would have had, simply left.
Over the 19th century, UK emigration averaged 0.5% of the population per year. About half of migrants eventually went to the US, with the remainder primarily going to Canada, Australia, New Zealand, with smaller numbers going to various African colonies, primarily what is now South Africa. In this post, I model a counterfactual where emigration of British citizens was zero since 1815, and compute the corresponding UK population.
Thanks for reading Model Thinking! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
Subscribe
Model and results
How can we estimate the population absent emigration? The naive solution—just add every emigrant back into the headcount—ignores the children those emigrants would have had. A cleaner method strips migration out of the growth rate itself: start with the observed population, subtract net migration each year as a share of the total, and let that adjusted growth rate compound forward. The result is a population path that implicitly assumes net migration is zero for the entire period.
2
The core emigration series was pieced together from
A History of Emigration
for 1815-1911 data,
some
1920s
Parliamentary questions on migration, a
statistics handbook
for 1948-1950, the post-1960 UK emigration records. Data for 1930-1947 was not readily available and was assumed to be zero for the sake of conservatism, and data for 1951-1960 was inferred from the net migration rate, meaning for both these periods actual outflows were likely notably higher. Data pre-1870 refers to every person who left via ports in Great Britain to emigrate to a long distance destination, and thus includes some individuals who transited through British ports for immigration purposes without being British themselves. Post-1870 data refers to British citizens only (or British subjects as they were known before 1949). Pre-1850 net migration was not available directly, and was imputed at 60% of the level of emigration, on the grounds that 40% of emigrants later permanently returned. All of Ireland is excluded from the data pre-1922, but post-1922 data includes Northern Ireland.
This methodology would imply a population of the UK today at slightly above 150mn. However, this ignores the potential effects of any emigration on fertility. Firstly, might there be some effect lowering the standard of living from the higher population, which could lower fertility? Under the classic Solow model of economic growth, this would occur, but not by much. The higher rate of population growth would depress the capital stock per capita - fewer machines per worker - reducing GDP per capita by about 4.7%.
3
Substantial, but not large enough to interrupt this population boom in its tracks. Secondly, the higher population would enable larger scale effects for cities - about 4% per doubling per Duranton and Puga (2020). If this larger population was sorted into cities at exactly the current distribution of size, this would by now have more than counteracted this decline, although it would have reduced fertility in the interim, and is hence included.
4
Additionally, a majority of migrants were male, causing a demographic imbalance in the UK - in 1850 there were 500k more women than men, implying 0.9% higher fertility in the 19th century without this (assuming monogamy).
Most of these effects are fairly small in magnitude however - adding up to a 5mn change in expected population. This is because the elasticity of fertility to income in the 18th century was fairly small -
Klemp (2012)
found 0.31 to wages, while
Foreman-Peck (2015)
found 0.13 and
Clark (2007)
found essentially zero - implying minimal changes in TFR given the already small changes in wages. 0.2 will be used here for the sake of conservativism.
The biggest upward revision comes from the emigrants’ own future families. Most left as adults: they had already survived the brutal childhood mortality of the 1800s, yet 80 % were still in the 15-50 age band, with the bulk clustering in th

data.title: The Inkhaven Blogging Residency
data.author: venkii
data.article_summary: 《墨水港》写作驻留项目招募30名优秀写作者，在11月期间每天发布一篇博客文章（否则将被淘汰）。项目位于加州伯克利，提供住宿，费用3500美元（含奖学金机会）。申请10天内出结果。导师团队包括多位知名作家，由Ben Pace等人组织。驻留时间为11月1日至30日。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对写作静修项目（residency）的评论和不同观点

不同观点：
• [habryka] 作为主办方代表，介绍了Lightcone Infrastructure及其相关项目（如LessWrong.com和Lighthaven.space），表示愿意回答任何相关问题，展现出对项目的高度参与和了解。

• [egypturnash] 表达了对项目费用（$3.5k）的羡慕与无奈，提到自己更愿意以较慢的节奏创作，同时通过计算自己每周创作的页数对比项目要求的字数，质疑了项目的实际工作量要求。

• [defrost] 通过历史类比，提到类似作家聚会的传统（如Inklings），指出历史上类似的活动成本很低（如酒吧喝酒），暗含对现代高费用静修项目的质疑。

• [cosmicgadget] 对参与者写出的作品表示兴趣，关注项目的实际成果。

• [netown] 将该项目比作博客界的Y-Combinator，但指出该项目要求前期学费而非投资，讨论了这种商业模式的可行性。

• [ajkjk] 认为该项目是千禧一代建立机构的例子，隐含对新兴社会机构建设的认可。

• [tenkabuto] 提到自己无法承担费用和时间成本，希望看到项目博客文章的汇总，表现出对远程参与的兴趣。

• [benwerd] 指出项目中隐含的意识形态（与Lesswrong社区相关），认为该社区的意识形态未必适合所有人，建议为持更人文主义观点的人创建类似项目。

• [tty456] 对项目的高费用提出批评，认为这是付费获得基本住宿特权，而非传统意义上的静修。

• [ttoinou] 质疑项目名称，认为这更像是一个“ retreat”（ retreat一般费用较低），并询问如何找到更多类似的写作活动，尤其是欧洲的。

• [TimorousBestie] 以幽默的方式表达了对参与者组合（Gwern和两个Scotts）的不解，暗示对项目参与者水平和匹配度的质疑。

• [miohtama] 提到AI提供的写作建议，暗示AI可能提供更便宜的替代方案。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于项目的高费用与其实际价值是否匹配，部分评论者对费用和项目命名提出质疑。
- 对项目隐含的意识形态和参与者水平存在不同看法，部分评论者希望有更多元化的项目形式和参与者背景。
- 一些评论者关注项目的实际成果和远程参与的可能性，表现出对项目成果的兴趣和需求。

data.title: DNA tests are uncovering the true prevalence of incest (2024)
data.author: georgecmu
data.article_summary: 文章讲述了史蒂夫·埃德塞尔（Steve Edsel）从小被养父母收养，他一直对自己的生母感到好奇。在14岁时，他开始真正思考自己的身世。20多岁时，他开始寻找生母，但线索中断。直到40岁，他决定再次尝试，并使用了AncestryDNA测试。在基因谱系专家CeCe Moore的帮助下，他发现生母可能是两名女性之一，最终确认是他的生母，且意外发现他的父母可能是近亲。Moore推测，他的父亲可能是生母的父亲或兄弟，这令史蒂夫震惊不已。文章还探讨了近亲繁殖在社会中的隐秘性和DNA测试揭示的此类案例的增多。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕遗传学、乱伦影响以及社会文化问题的讨论

不同观点：
• [robertlagrant] 认为，文章中提到的数字只是最低值，因为这些数字仅包括导致怀孕、未流产并最终生下成年后参与研究的人。他还指出，如果某人的DNA在UK Biobank中，可能更有可能患有因乱伦导致的遗传疾病。
• [fsflover] 对在Facebook上创建私人支持小组的做法表示担忧，认为由于Facebook的隐私政策，这不是一个理想的选择。
• [nineplay] 提出，许多被羞辱为“小镇荡妇”的女性实际上是性虐待的受害者。他们认为，社会往往忽视了这些女性所遭受的侵害，而将责任归咎于性教育不足。
• [DoctorOetker] 提供了详细的遗传学解释，说明如果父母是近亲，遗传缺陷的风险会增加。同时也指出，如果后代与基因健康的人繁育，遗传疾病负担会迅速减少。此外，还讨论了遗传学以外的“模因学”，即思想和观点的传播和重组。
• [searine] 认为，更大的问题是一些地方对近亲关系的文化接受度较高。

补充讨论：
• [Mistletoe] 表达了不愿意阅读可能令人不安的文章，希望有人能提供具体百分比。
• [gaoryrt] 通过数学计算指出，如果父母及其父母都不是近亲，那么在第30代时，祖先的数量将达到约10.7亿，这表明远祖的多样性。

When Steve Edsel was a boy, his adoptive parents kept a scrapbook of newspaper clippings in their bedroom closet. He would ask for it sometimes, poring over the headlines about his birth. Headlines like this: “Mother Deserts Son, Flees From Hospital,”
Winston-Salem Journal,
December 30, 1973.
The mother in question was 14 years old, “5 feet 6 with reddish brown hair,” and she had come to the hospital early one morning with her own parents. They gave names that all turned out to be fake. And by 8 o’clock that evening, just hours after she gave birth, they were gone. In a black-and-white drawing of the mother, based on nurses’ recollections, she has round glasses and sideswept bangs. Her mouth is grimly set.
The abandoned boy was placed in foster care with a local couple, the Edsels, who later adopted him. Steve knew all of this growing up. His parents never tried to hide his origins, and they always gave him the scrapbook when he asked. It wasn’t until he turned 14, though, that he really began to wonder about his birth mom. “I’m 14,” he thought at the time. “This is how old she was when she had me.”
Steve began looking for her in earnest in his 20s, but the paper trail quickly ran cold. When he turned 40, he told his wife, Michelle, that he wanted to give the search one last go. This was in 2013. AncestryDNA had started selling mail-in test kits the previous year, so he bought one. His matches at first seemed unpromising—some distant relatives—but when he began posting in a Facebook group for people seeking out biological family, he got connected to a genetic genealogist named CeCe Moore. Moore specializes in finding people via distant DNA matches, a technique made famous in 2018 when it led to the
capture of the Golden State Killer
. But back then, genetic genealogy was still new, and Moore was one of its pioneers. She volunteered to help Steve.
Within just a couple of weeks, she had narrowed down the search to two women, cousins of the same age. On Facebook, Steve could see that one cousin had four kids, and she regularly posted photos of them, beautiful and smiling. They looked well-off, their lives picture-perfect—“like a storybook,” Steve says. The other woman was unmarried; she didn’t have kids. She was not friends with her immediate family on Facebook, and she had moved halfway across the country from them. One evening—a Saturday, Steve clearly remembers—Moore asked to speak with him by phone.
She confirmed what he had already suspected: His birth mom was the second woman. But Moore had another piece of news too. She had unexpectedly figured out something about his biological father as well.
It looks like your parents are related.
Steve didn’t know what to say.
Do you understand what I mean?
He said he thought so.
Either your mom’s father or your mom’s brother is your father.
A sea of emotions rose to a boil inside him: anger, hurt, worthlessness, disgust, shame, and devastation all at once. In his years of wondering about his birth, he had never, ever considered the possibility of incest. Why would he? What were the chances?
In 1975, around the time of Steve’s birth, a psychiatric textbook put the frequency of incest at one in a million.
But this number is almost certainly a dramatic underestimate. The stigma around openly discussing incest, which often involves child sexual abuse, has long made the subject difficult to study. In the 1980s,
feminist scholars argued
, based on the testimonies of victims, that incest was far more common than recognized, and in recent years, DNA has offered a new kind of biological proof. Widespread genetic testing is uncovering case after secret case of children born to close biological relatives—providing an unprecedented accounting of incest in modern society.
The geneticist Jim Wilson, at the University of Edinburgh, was shocked by the frequency he found in the U.K. Biobank, an anonymized research database: One in 7,000 people, according to his unpublished analysis, was born to parents who were first-degree relatives—a brother and a sister or a parent and a child. “That’s way, way more than I think many people would ever imagine,” he told me. And this number is just a floor: It reflects only the cases that resulted in pregnancy, that did not end in miscarriage or abortion, and that led to the birth of a child who grew into an adult who volunteered for a research study.
Most of the people affected may never know about their parentage, but these days, many are stumbling into the truth after AncestryDNA and 23andMe tests. Steve’s case was one of the first Moore worked on involving closely related parents. She now knows of well over 1,000 additional cases of people born from incest, the significant majority between first-degree relatives, with the rest between second-degree relatives (half-siblings, uncle-niece, aunt-nephew, grandparent-grandchild). The cases show up in every part of society, every strata of i

• [DoctorOetker] 提供了详细的遗传学解释，说明如果父母是近亲，遗传缺陷的风险会增加。同时也指出，如果后代与基因健康的人繁育，遗传疾病负担会迅速减少。此外，还讨论了遗传学以外的“模因学”，即思想和观点的传播和重组。
• [searine] 认为，更大的问题是一些地方对近亲关系的文化接受度较高。

补充讨论：
• [Mistletoe] 表达了不愿意阅读可能令人不安的文章，希望有人能提供具体百分比。
• [gaoryrt] 通过数学计算指出，如果父母及其父母都不是近亲，那么在第30代时，祖先的数量将达到约10.7亿，这表明远祖的多样性。
• [ChrisArchitect] 提供了一个相关讨论的链接，引导读者查看另一个讨论平台上的内容。
• [toomuchtodo] 提供了一个存档链接，但没有进一步评论。

• 关于Facebook隐私问题的讨论，[fslover]对在Facebook上创建私人支持小组表示质疑。

data.title: Tribblix – The Retro Illumos Distribution
data.author: bilegeek
data.article_summary: Tribblix是一个由Peter Tribble开发的开源操作系统，基于illumos，融合了复古风格和现代组件。2025年7月13日发布了Milestone 37，提供Vanilla Tribblix和LX变体（x86版本）以及相关更新。SPARC版本也从m32升级到m33，但建议先安装m32再升级。2025年5月15日发布了适用于m32 SPARC的CDROM大小ISO。注意，系统已完全移除32位硬件支持。x86版本相对稳定，而SPARC版本的硬件支持仍不完善。更多信息和下载可访问其官网。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同操作系统及其在现代硬件上的应用和兼容性问题

不同观点：
• rollcat认为一些小众但功能齐全的操作系统（如Tribblix、Dragonfly BSD、Haiku、RISC OS、9front、MINIX）值得关注，它们存在了几十年但通常不被广泛注意。

• shrubble强调了Solaris Zones（容器）和LX zones（Linux容器）在同一硬件上运行的实用性，并提到在USB3处理上遇到的问题，例如在AMD 8350系统上因为XHCI问题无法从USB安装，建议通过烧录CD解决。

• Crontab对Illumos中的ZFS版本与OpenZFS的兼容性表示好奇，询问是否会与Linux/FreeBSD系统上的OpenZFS不兼容。

• gr4vityWall认为Illumos家族很有趣，但难以在现代硬件上安装，尝试过OpenIndiana、Tribblix和OmniOS都未能成功。建议创建Linux驱动程序的兼容层以提高UNIX内核的可用性，并提到Oxide可能有相关经验。

• 0xCafeBabee比喻维护旧系统比维护旧车还难，暗示旧系统的维护成本高且困难。

• hulitu对未将CDE和OpenLook作为首选桌面环境表示惊讶，并指出系统从支持32位硬件到完全移除32位支持的变化。

补充讨论：
• rollcat提到的小众操作系统在技术爱好者和特定应用场景中的持续吸引力。
• shrubble提出的USB安装问题显示了旧系统在现代硬件兼容性上的挑战。
• Crontab的问题涉及到ZFS文件系统在不同操作系统之间的兼容性，这是一个技术细节和实用性上的关注点。
• gr4vityWall对兼容层的建议反映了对提高旧操作系统在现代硬件上可用性的技术探讨。
• hulitu对桌面环境和硬件支持变化的评论显示了对传统系统变化的不适应。

争议焦点：
• 小众操作系统在现代应用中的实用性和安装难度是讨论中的主要争议点。
• ZFS版本兼容性问题也是技术用户关注的焦点。
• 对桌面环境选择的期望差异反映了用户对传统和现代界面选择的不同偏好。

data.title: Representing Python notebooks as dataflow graphs
data.author: akshayka
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了一种新型的开源Python笔记本工具——marimo，它通过数据流图（dataflow graphs）来解决传统笔记本（如Jupyter）在可重复性、交互性、可维护性和可重用性方面的问题。传统笔记本容易积累隐藏状态，导致代码和输出不同步，影响可重复性。此外，它们的JSON格式使得版本控制和代码重用困难。marimo将笔记本表示为数据流图，集成了反应式计算，能保持代码和输出的同步，并支持将笔记本作为可执行脚本、Python模块和交互式Web应用使用。这种设计提升了AI和数据工作的效率和可靠性。marimo旨在解决传统笔记本的不足，提供更具交互性、可维护性和重用性的解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Marimo及其他类似笔记本工具的优缺点，特别是在可重复性、复杂性、以及对不同用户群体的适用性方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• [支持Marimo] data-ottawa认为Marimo极大地提升了工作流的效率，尤其是通过UV和沙盒功能，能更容易地与团队分享笔记本。他们赞赏Marimo团队的快速响应和高质量软件开发。虽然有些问题与Python库（如graphviz）有关，但总体体验非常好。对于长时间运行的计算，虽然有功能帮助（如添加运行按钮），但有时需要关闭自动运行，这降低了反应式流程的价值。

• [反对复杂工具] Galanwe认为这些工具（如Marimo）试图解决笔记本的可重复性问题，但增加了复杂性。他指出，稍有经验的用户会通过"重启内核并运行所有"来确保笔记本的可重复性，而新手用户则会因复杂性而却步。因此，他认为这些工具只对有"救世主情结"的开发者有用，而不会被普通研究用户广泛接受。

• [外行质疑] philsnow作为笔记本生态系统的外行，对笔记本存在过期中间结果表示惊讶，认为这是一个显而易见且应早已解决的问题。他质疑是否由于缺乏跨领域交流导致此问题持续存在。

• [折中立场] getnormality认为保持笔记本的可重复性并不困难，只需通过简单的复制和运行检查即可。虽然大数据和慢反馈 loop 可能增加难度，但通过类似RStudio的命令历史功能可以缓解。他承认Marimo看起来不错，但笔记本如果被完全信任可能带来危险。

• [支持结构化代码] tastyminerals2赞赏Marimo的响应式执行和变量去重功能，认为它有助于写出结构更好的Python代码，是一种胜利。

• [与其他工具比较] nylonstrung认为Marimo类似于Streamlit或Observable，如果喜欢这些工具，Marimo也会是一个不错的选择。

• [对执行模型的批评] riedel指出笔记本的执行模型仍然令人困惑，即使是数据流扩展如ipyflow也无法完全解决。他建议采用类似编译器的DAG和SSA形式，并认为笔记本界面需要调整以支持更复杂的控制流。

• [关于外部系统的讨论] PeterStuer提问是否需要对接触Python外部系统的代码进行"volatile"标记。

• [对数据管道的担忧] probablypower认为虽然文章写得很好，但将笔记本嵌入数据管道存在潜在问题，表示不赞同。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点主要在于笔记本工具（如Marimo）是否真正解决了可重复性问题，还是只是增加了复杂性。
• 对笔记本执行模型的批评与建议，如采用类似编译器的DAG结构，显示出对笔记本功能更深层次的思考。
• 不同用户群体（新手、有经验的用户、开发者）对工具的需求和接受度的差异也是讨论的重要方面。

August 4, 2025
Python notebooks as dataflow graphs: reactive, reproducible, and reusable
Akshay
@
akshaykagrawal
This blog is adapted from our talk at PyCon 2025. marimo is free and open
source, available on
GitHub
. For
a free online experience with link sharing, try
molab
.
marimo is a new kind of open-source Python notebook. While traditional
notebooks are just REPLs, marimo notebooks are Python programs represented as
dataflow graphs. This intermediate representation lets marimo
blend the best parts of interactive computing with the reproducibility and
reusability of Python software: every marimo notebook works as a reactive
notebook for Python (and SQL) that keeps code and outputs in sync (run a cell
and marimo knows which other cells to run), an executable script and a Python
module, and an interactive web app.
In this blog post, we motivate the need for a new kind of notebook, explain how
and why marimo represents notebooks as dataflow graphs, present design
decisions we made to help users adapt to dataflow programming, discuss
our implementation, and show several examples of how marimo uses its dataflow
graph to make data work reactive, interactive, reproducible, and reusable.
Contents.
Motivating a new kind of notebook
marimo: a new kind of notebook
Representation as a dataflow graph
How marimo uses the dataflow graph
Implementation
Conclusion
Motivating a new kind of notebook
AI and data work are different from software engineering.
When you work with data, it’s helpful to hold objects in memory,
iteratively transforming and visualizing them as you evaluate
datasets, models, and algorithms. Notebooks are the only programming
environment that enable this workflow — for this reason, the number of GitHub
repos with Jupyter notebooks
more than doubled in
2024
,
alongside the rise of AI.
Interactive computing is crucial for evaluating
data and algorithms. These GIFs visualize projected LBFGS
applied to different embedding formulations on the MNIST dataset.
I made them in Jupyter notebooks during my PhD in machine learning;
I used Jupyter notebooks extensively during my PhD, but I also had
issues in reproducibility, interactivity, maintainability, and reusability,
which motivated me to start work on marimo.
Nonetheless, traditional notebooks such as Google Colab or Jupyter notebooks
suffer from issues in reproducibility, interactivity, maintainability, and
reusability, making them unsuited for modern AI and data work and creating
the need for a new kind of notebook.
Reproducibility
Traditional notebooks have a reproducibility crisis. In
2019, a
study
from New
York University and Federal Fluminense University found that of the nearly
1 million Jupyter notebooks on GitHub with valid execution orders, only 24%
could be re-run, and just 4% reproduced the same results. A
similar
study
from 2020 by JetBrains found that over a third of the notebooks on GitHub had
invalid execution histories.
Traditional notebooks accumulate hidden state: run or delete a cell,
and program memory is imperatively mutated without regard to the rest of the
code on the page. This allows code and outputs to become out of sync. While a feature of
REPLs, hidden state gets in the way when you’re trying to do work you’d like to
reproduce.
Code and outputs in traditional notebooks
can become out of sync
These studies can be scrutinized and caveated, but the finding resonates with
developer sentiment at large, not to mention my own experience as a former
machine learning PhD student who used notebooks on an almost daily basis.
You
have to be very disciplined
to make a
Jupyter notebook that is actually reproducible. At least for the
kind of work that I do, I’d prefer a tool that was reproducible by default.
Interactivity
While Jupyter notebooks are interactive in that you can execute cells
iteratively,
data
in traditional notebooks is not interactive. As a
researcher, I wanted to make selections in scatter plots and get my selection
back as a dataframe automatically. These kinds of highly interactive
experiences were simply out of reach.
Maintainability
Jupyter’s JSON file format and the fact that
Jupyter notebooks are not well-formed programs makes code reuse difficult.
Because traditional notebooks are not Python files but instead stored with code
and outputs serialized in what
Pydantic creator Samuel Colvin calls a “horrid
blob”
of JSON, they are difficult to
maintain. Instead of reusing code, practitioners end up duplicating notebooks
or starting from scratch. (The file format also makes it hard to version
notebooks with Git.)
Reusability
Finally, because traditional notebooks aren’t guaranteed to be valid Python
programs, they are difficult to reuse as data pipelines, as apps, or software.
And yet people try anyway (just look at Databricks and SageMaker), because
AI and data
people really like interactive programming environments
.
marimo: a new kind of notebook
Toward the end of my PhD, I got to thinking:
what would it t

data.title: Sandstorm- self-hostable web productivity suite
data.author: nalinidash
data.article_summary: Sandstorm是一个开源项目，旨在简化运行开源网络应用程序的过程。它提供文档编辑（Etherpad）、文件存储（Davros）、任务与项目管理（Wekan）以及安全聊天（Rocket.Chat）等功能。与传统方法不同，Sandstorm安装应用非常简便，类似于在手机上安装应用，并提供自动更新和统一的访问控制。每个应用和数据都默认私密，通过“grain”机制进行安全隔离，有效缓解95%的安全漏洞。用户可选择云端或自建服务器托管数据，且可以在不同选项间自由切换。Sandstorm适合个人、企业和开发者使用，个人用户可增强安全性与隐私保护，企业可集中管理数据并提高生产力，开发者则可轻松发布和管理应用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Sandstorm 项目的现状、优缺点以及与其他自托管平台的比较。

不同观点：
• **AceJohnny2** 回顾了 Sandstorm 的历史，提到其最初通过 Indiegogo 众筹推出，随后因资金问题导致开发团队解散，目前由社区接手开发。他还提到项目创始人 Kenton Varda 目前在 Cloudflare 工作，并提供了相关链接。
• **germandiago** 分享了自己使用 Sandstorm 的实际经验，认为其在项目管理和自托管文档方面表现出色，但包生态系统缺乏维护。他正在考虑迁移到 Yunohost，但希望找到类似的、易于维护的平台。
• **raphinou** 表示自己最终选择了 Docker Swarm 作为自托管解决方案，认为其设置简单、维护成本低，并且许多项目提供兼容的 Docker Compose 文件。
• **bhasinanant** 对 Sandstorm 和 NextCloud 进行了比较，质疑前者的功能集和使用理由，尽管他支持本地化设置。
• **c-hendricks** 回忆 Sandstorm 最初是一个带有自托管应用和集成认证层的平台，管理用户和权限较为容易，但他选择了 Authelia 作为替代方案。
• **kentonv** 作为创始人，说明了 Sandstorm 项目的现状，承认其目前的状态不佳，建议不要在当前状态下使用。但他同时提到 Sandstorm 的架构在某些方面仍然具有相关性，并暗示可能会重新参与开发。
• **meindnoch** 对 Sandstorm 是否仍然存在和是否有人使用表示怀疑，并询问其使用案例。
• **docsaintly** 也曾考虑过 Sandstorm，但最终选择了 Cloudron，认为后者在应用选择和安全性方面表现更好。
• **MissTake** 指出 Sandstorm 缺乏维护，问题堆积且少有代码更改，认为投入时间在此平台上不值得。

补充讨论：
• **esafak** 提出希望有更小的图片和更大的截图。
• **oulipo** 询问 Sandstorm 与 Dokploy 等工具的区别。

争议焦点：
• Sandstorm 是否仍然具有实用性和维护价值。
• 与其他自托管平台（如 Yunohost、Cloudron、Docker Swarm）相比，Sandstorm 的优劣势。

总结：讨论主要围绕 Sandstorm 的历史、现状、功能及其与其他自托管解决方案的比较。用户对 Sandstorm 的维护状态和实用性存在不同看法，部分用户对其前景表示担忧并考虑迁移到其他平台。创始人的回应也为项目的未来带来了一定的不确定性和期待。

44844394.article_content:
Self-host web apps easily and securely.
Sandstorm is an open source project built by a community of volunteers with the goal of making
it really easy to run open source web applications.
Document Editing
Create, edit, and collaborate on documents with Etherpad.
File Storage
Store all your files and share them with others using Davros.
Task & Project Management
Organize all your tasks and ideas using Wekan.
Chat
Sync up with your colleagues securely using Rocket.Chat.
Online Demo
Get it now
Check out the apps available on Sandstorm »
How is it different?
Installing apps on Sandstorm is as easy as installing apps on your phone.
Find any app you want on the App Market and start using it with a few clicks. Every app comes with automatic updates.
All your apps and data in one place, with consistent access control.
Sandstorm keeps a list so you can find everything you create. Sandstorm's unified access control system covers data from every app, and everything is private to you by default.
Sandstorm protects you.
Each document, chat room, mail box, notebook, blog, or anything else you create is a "grain" in Sandstorm. Sandstorm containerizes each one in its own secure sandbox from which it cannot talk to the world without express permission. All your grains are private until you share them. The result is that 95% of security vulnerabilities are automatically mitigated.
Skeptical? Learn more about
Sandstorm's security model
and
security non-events
.
Sandstorm makes it easy to adhere to security, regulatory, and data privacy requirements.
Sandstorm manages access control on every document, so it can show who has access and allow you to revoke that access at any time. Self-hosting Sandstorm enables organizations to have complete control over where their data is stored.
You choose where your data lives:
You can use Sandstorm in the cloud on a variety of hosting services, or you can
install it on your own machines.
You can even move between these options at any time. No matter where you decide to run Sandstorm, the apps are the same.
With Sandstorm, you do not get locked into walled gardens.
You can mix and match apps from multiple developers with ease, and even throw in apps of your own as needed. Many Sandstorm apps are open source, which means you can modify them to suit you needs.
Who is it for?
Individuals
Sandstorm makes it safe & easy to use open source web apps. It adds security hardening and protects your privacy. Apps never disappear, and you can add your own. Run your
own server.
Learn More
Businesses
Sandstorm lets you keep all your company's data in one place, rather than scattered across dozens of web apps. At the same time, it lets each team in your company choose their own tools and deploy applications to meet their needs, without having to file tickets and wait for support from other teams. This makes your employees more productive while keeping your data safe and under control.
Learn More
Developers
Ship your code as a Sandstorm app package and don't worry about how to run a service or scale it up. On Sandstorm, independent developers, hobbyists, and open source projects can build quality applications that people can actually use, without worrying about how to run a service.
Learn More

data.title: Car has more than 1.2M km on it – and it's still going strong
data.author: Sgt_Apone
data.article_summary:
安迪·坎贝尔（Andy Campbell）是一位来自新斯科舍省的居民，他拥有一辆1985年产的丰田Tercel，这辆车已经行驶了超过125万公里，相当于往返月球1.5次或绕地球31圈。尽管车上的里程表显示只有253,070公里，但实际上少显示了100万公里。坎贝尔在1990年以2,500美元购买了这辆车，当时它的里程数为125,000公里。他每天驾驶这辆车往返于住处和工作地点，如今退休后仍用它来出行和办事。

尽管几乎所有部件都已被更换或修理，坎贝尔坚持定期维护，自己动手进行大部分保养。他有三辆备用Tercel用于更换零件。他还有一辆1986年产的Tercel作为备用车辆。坎贝尔对这辆车的热爱源于其实用性、雪天驾驶的优越性能以及低维护成本。他表示，自己并不是特别喜欢车，只是特别钟情于这辆Tercel。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：车辆的耐用性、维修性以及环保影响

不同观点：
• **关于车辆耐用性和维修性**：
  - [1970-01-01] 认为旧车型设计简单，易于维修，而2000年后车辆虽然更耐用，但维修难度增加，特别是"终身"部件的更换可能需要更多时间和精力。
  - [physix] 以1990年代德国柴油奔驰出租车为例，指出当时车辆的高耐用性，许多车辆能行驶超过百万公里，但认为现在的奔驰不再有过去的质量。
  - [SilverElfin] 认为如果车辆所有部件都被更换过，很难判断车辆的真正耐用性，并对这种情况下车辆的吸引力提出质疑。

• **关于现代车辆与老旧车辆的对比**：
  - [jbeard4] 提出“Theseus之车”的问题：如果车辆所有部件都被更换，它还是同一辆车吗？
  - [63] 认为如果通过更换发动机来延长车辆寿命，这是一个耗时且费钱的过程，并对新闻报道的真实性提出质疑。
  - [mitkebes] 提到特斯拉也有车辆达到了高里程数，暗示现代电动车也具备高耐用性。

• **关于环保和经济性**：
  - [franze] 引用“祖父的斧头”故事，暗示不断更换部件以维持车辆运行，可能削弱其原有的独特性和价值。
  - [jfengel] 认为在某些情况下，放弃旧车购买新车可能更划算，并且在环境成本上相差不大，尽管劳动成本较高。
  - [mrweasel] 提出政府不仅应禁止销售新的内燃机汽车，还应禁止寿命低于15-20年的汽车销售，认为这可能对环境更有利。

补充讨论：
• **品牌讨论**：
  - [cpursley] 和 [paffdragon] 提到丰田和Škoda的高里程车辆，暗示某些品牌的车辆天然具备更高的耐用性。
  - [Matterless] 对比丰田和日产，指出丰田车辆更耐用，而自己的日产车在10万公里时就接近报废，特别提到对CVT变速箱的不满。

• **个人经历**：
  - [nickd2001] 分享朋友根据车辆外观和收音机设置来判断车况并成功购买可靠二手车的经历，强调了车主行为对车辆维护的影响。
  - [petee] 提到SAAB品牌过去很容易达到高里程数，并指出过去的车辆更容易维护。

争议焦点：
• 车辆在所有部件被更换后是否还能视为同一辆车，涉及到耐用性与维修性的平衡问题。
• 是否应该通过立法限制车辆寿命以促进环保，涉及到经济性与环境影响之间的权衡。

44806422.article_content:
Nova Scotia
This car has more than 1.2 million km on it — and it's still going strong
Andy Campbell's 1985 Toyota Tercel has travelled the equivalent of 1.5 round trips to the moon.
1985 Toyota Tercel has travelled the equivalent of 1.5 round trips to the moon
Frances Willick
·
CBC News
·
Posted: Aug 05, 2025 5:00 AM EDT | Last Updated: August 5
What makes this 1985 Toyota Tercel so unique?
4 days ago
Duration
2:52
A Nova Scotia man is the proud owner of a 1985 Toyota Tercel. Despite being 40 years old, the car is in mint condition. But there is one thing wrong with it: the odometer doesn't go up high enough. The CBC's Frances Willick explains.
Social Sharing
If you were to spot Andy Campbell's ride on the road, you might not think too much about it.
Maybe you'd think it's a bit dated — a throwback to an earlier time when cassette tapes were all the rage and backup cameras were just a glimmer in a car designer's eye.
But if you took a closer look, you'd see that there's something special about Campbell's 1985 Toyota Tercel.
It's not just that it runs perfectly, or that it's practically in mint condition.
The only thing wrong with this Tercel is that the odometer doesn't go up high enough.
It reads 253,070. But it's missing a one. As in, one million.
This car has 1,253,070 kilometres on it — and counting.
The odometer on the vehicle shows 253,070 kilometres, but in reality it's been driven 1,253,070 kilometres.
(Frances Willick/CBC)
That's more than three times the distance to the moon, or enough kilometres to drive around the Earth 31 times.
And Campbell has the photos to prove it. When it turned over from 999,999 kilometres to 000,000 kilometres in September 2017, he pulled over to the side of the road to snap some photos. Now, he keeps them in his glove compartment as proof in case there are any doubters.
Andy Campbell bought the Tercel around 1990, when it had 125,000 kilometres on it.
(Brian MacKay/CBC)
Campbell bought the '85 Tercel in Halifax around 1990, paying $2,500 for the vehicle with about 125,000 kilometres on it.
Since then, he's used it as his daily driver, putting on at least 120 kilometres a day driving from his home in Wyses Corner, N.S., to Halifax and back each day of his working life.
Now retired, he still uses it to run errands or boot around the Maritimes, or even as far afield as Newfoundland.
Campbell says although his vehicle has seen its share of pavement, he's never taken it outside of Atlantic Canada.
(Brian MacKay/CBC)
Although the Tercel is old enough to qualify for antique plates, Campbell doesn't want them, as they would restrict his ability to use it for everyday purposes.
"You go to a car show and the people drive the cars to the show and they polish it and take it home and put it in the garage and cover it over," he says. "That car is for me to use. If I gotta get up in a snowstorm and go to Halifax or Elmsdale or whatever it might be, I can go with it."
His own best mechanic
Over the years, nearly everything on the vehicle has been replaced or repaired, and Campbell says the only original part is likely the body, and even that has had work done on it.
Aside from the front-end alignment, he does all the work himself, relying on his sizable stash of parts, most of which are no longer available from Toyota. He's got three more Tercels up on blocks at the back of his property, just in case he needs something.
Campbell has three old Tercels up on blocks that he uses for parts.
(Frances Willick/CBC)
"It looks like junk and to most people, it probably is," he says.
But to him, it's gold.
Campbell has every part imaginable tucked away, including multiples of most.
(Frances Willick/CBC)
He says the key to keeping a car running for a long time is to do regular maintenance such as oil changes and lubrication, and to undercoat the vehicle. A heated garage doesn't hurt, either, he says.
Campbell acknowledges that Tercels have a reputation for being "rust buckets," but says his secret is to fill all of the crevices with grease. "They've got pumped every one of them right full."
Backup ride
If his Tercel is temporarily out of commission for maintenance, Campbell does have a backup.
"Would you like to see my new car?" he asks.
The garage door opens, and an identical Tercel pulls out.
"This is my new one — '86," he says, grinning.
Campbell's backup ride is also a Tercel — an '86, which he calls his 'new' car.
(Frances Willick/CBC)
Campbell says he's not really a car guy. He's not a Toyota guy, or even a Tercel guy.
He's a
his Tercel
guy.
He's passionate about his vehicle because it's practical, great in the snow, easy to maintain and cheap to operate.
"Everybody can pass me on the road but I get to pass them at the service station," he says.
Campbell does almost all of the maintenance on his vehicles.
(Frances Willick/CBC)
Campbell is not the only Tercel long-hauler in the province.
Jim George of Kentville also has an '85 Tercel, but it's a mere babe in the woods compared to Campbell's,

data.title: A SPARC makes a little fire
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者在2018年试图修复一台Sun SparcStation 1+工作站的经历。机器启动时总是报"Illegal Instruction"错误，作者尝试了多种方法诊断问题：移除硬盘发现错误信息变化，插入原装苹果SCSI硬盘（ID设为0）却不识别，后发现Sun固件会将SCSI ID 0重定向到3。作者还尝试了其他SCSI硬盘组合，但均未成功，甚至无硬盘时系统也会挂起。最后考虑使用软驱启动Linux或BSD来进一步诊断，但全文以一系列未解决的硬件兼容性问题作结，展现了复古计算机维修的挑战性。

44799929.article_content:
Way back in May of 2018,
I was unable to get the SparcStation 1+ to stop returning “Illegal Instruction” errors for any attempt at booting
. This made absolutely no sense to anyone I asked about it, and they suggested replacing the PROM battery, because at least then we’d have fewer known-broken parts in the computer. I ignored this advice, and just stuck the computer in a corner with the other broken machines for awhile so it could think about what it did.
A few weekends later, I decided to go back and give the little Sun another chance. Perhaps it was the cute pizzabox appearance, or maybe it was that I needed to clear the bench space for something else.
To begin diagnosis, I yanked the hard drive out, and discovered the Quantum ProDrive in it was in fact an Apple factory drive. Here’s the badge, indicating that the drive was shipped with an
Apple ROM
.
Looks like it has some pins for a hard drive access LED. Considering it’s a full-height drive, I wonder which Mac this would have come out of. Maybe an early SE or II? Definitely not an LC.
A lot of early Apple hard drives are hardcoded to SCSI ID 0, and while they have pins to reset them, they don’t come with jumpers (I realized this was since the three jumpers set the SCSI ID
in binary
, which should have been obvious to me before - no jumpers = all false = 0). As far as I can tell, this one is the same way.
I decided to boot it without a hard drive installed at all. Maybe that would give me a cooler error than “Illegal Instruction!”
It did - the computer decided to try and boot off the loopback device instead, and when it failed, it didn’t say “illegal instruction.” What’s more, I could now type
boot sd(0,0,0)vmunix
without getting Illegal Instruction either!
I immediately slammed the drive back in and tried to boot. This time, I just got a
SCSI device is not responding
error. Assuming the drive was dead, I began my usual Quantum ProDrive diagnostic method of:
Feeling the drive for vibrations that indicate it is working,
Tapping the drive gently with the handle of a screwdriver,
Tapping the drive less gently with the handle of a screwdriver,
Repeatedly trying to start the drive until I hear it finally come to life.
Eventually, the drive started making noise and vibrating, so I assumed it was fully alive. This was not the case, as I would find out later, but it didn’t matter.
I looked online for information about the “not responding” error, and found one Usenet post from 1995. In it, the protagonist had a similar machine (an IPX) that wouldn’t boot, but was able to boot it using
boot sd(0,3,0)vmunix
instead of the default ID of 0.
That’s weird, since
probe-scsi
was pretty adamant the drive was target 0, device 0. Some more searching revealed that, yeah, the SparcStation firmware reroutes ID 0 to ID 3 for some reason only understood by Sun engineers and/or the legally insane (pay attention - this comes up again later.) OK, whatever… let’s try it.
Now I got an even better error message -
bad magic number in disk label
. I assume that this is telling me that the firmware doesn’t understand the partition map of the disk.
That error message was followed by a complaint that I had pointed the computer at a non-executable file, which makes sense, since not being able to read the partition map generally makes it difficult to find any files.
More disks! More parts! More problems!
To check if I could magically make this thing start working by adding more variables to the problem, I did a little bit of disk swapping. In went a second SCSI disk from my collection, a 2.2GB Quantum Viking that I found in a greasy shoebox. While this drive is supposedly a little big for the older firmware to support, it should at least be
detected
by
probe-scsi
as a SCSI device.
The following table describes my findings:
Viking in Left Bay
ProDrive in Left Bay
Nothing in Left Bay
Viking in Right Bay
N/A
“SCSI bus hung”
“Bad magic number”
ProDrive in Right Bay
Hangs after banner
N/A
“Bad magic number”
Nothing in Right Bay
Hangs after banner
“Bad magic number”
Hangs after banner
Hanging the SCSI bus wasn’t too big of a surprise in retrospect, since both drives are set to ID 0 from the factory and would of course conflict. I was not thinking awfully clearly back in 2018 when I was doing this, apparently.
What surprised me is that putting the Viking in bay 1 locked up the machine, and so did not having any disks at all. I thought this was supposed to be a diskless-capable workstation.
Nothing was adding up.
Floppy drives exist, right?
There is one more thing the SparcStation 1+ has up its sleeve: an auto-eject floppy drive. Like the Macintoshes, ejecting the floppy is driven by software, which is a feature that sounds really boring but is actually cool in person. Much like this entire machine. At least a Macintosh got to
eject floppy disks in outer space
.
In theory, I could make a Linux or BSD boot floppy and boot off it. Then I could use the booted-from operating system’s disk tools to lo

data.title: Additional Intel Linux Kernel Drivers Left Orphaned and Maintainers Let Go
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: Intel的全面重组导致更多Linux驱动程序被遗弃，维护者离职。近日，多个补丁将Intel的一些驱动程序标记为无人维护，并移除了已离开Intel的Linux开发者的维护者条目。其中包括Intel Ethernet RDMA驱动程序的共同维护者Mustafa Ismail离职，Intel PTP DFL ToD驱动程序的维护者Tianfei Zhang离职，导致这些驱动程序无人维护。此外，Intel WWAN IOSM驱动也因维护者M Chetan Kumar的离职而无人维护，尽管该驱动仍在内核中，但可能因缺乏维护而被移除。其他如Intel Keem Bay DRM驱动和T7XX 5G WWAN驱动的维护者也已离开公司。这些变动反映了Intel在某些技术领域的退出及其对开源社区的影响。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Intel削减开支对Linux用户的影响，特别是WiFi芯片的支持。

不同观点：

补充讨论：
• 评论中提到了对未来Intel硬件支持的担忧，特别是Linux用户可能面临的选择问题。如果Intel减少对开源社区的支持，可能会导致其硬件在Linux环境中的使用体验下降，从而影响用户对Intel产品的选择。
• 另一个讨论点是关于削减开支的必要性及其可能带来的负面影响。虽然削减开支可能是公司生存和发展的需要，但其对不同用户群体的影响，尤其是对依赖于特定支持的Linux用户，可能导致用户对Intel品牌信任度的下降。
• 争议焦点在于，Intel是否会在削减开支的同时，继续保持对开源社区和Linux用户的支持。这关系到用户对Intel硬件未来兼容性和安全性的信心。

44844324.article_content:
Additional Intel Linux Drivers Left Orphaned & Maintainers Let Go
Written by
Michael Larabel
in
Intel
on 8 August 2025 at 04:32 PM EDT.
27 Comments
Well, it's an unpleasant afternoon in Linux land with more signs of the ongoing impact from Intel's corporate-wide restructuring. Just after writing about
Intel's CPU temperature monitoring driver now left unmaintained/orphaned
, more patches hit the public Linux kernel mailing list to mark additional Intel drivers as orphaned and removing maintainer entries for Linux developers no longer at Intel.
One of the new patches
today
drops one of the maintainers of the Intel Ethernet RDMA driver. The Intel Ethernet RDMA driver is still maintained as one other Intel engineer was serving as co-maintainer but Mustafa Ismail is no longer at Intel.
One of the other Linux drivers now orphaned is the Intel PTP DFL ToD driver. This follows other
recent Intel FPGA DFL maintainer changes
. The Intel FPGA DFL ToD driver is for the time-of-day device on their FPGA cards.
This patch
marks the Intel PTP DFL ToD driver as orphaned with Tianfei Zhang no longer at Intel.
The Intel WWAN IOSM driver is one of the other drivers now
orphaned
by today's patches. This comes as maintainer M Chetan Kumar is no longer at Intel. Intel exited the WWAN and modem business several years ago so this orphaning isn't entirely surprising but unfortunate for anyone that might still have an Intel M.2 modem in use. This driver was in use by some Chromebook devices too beyond conventional Linux laptop/desktop use. The driver is being left in the kernel for now at least but could be subject to bit-rot and eventual removal without anyone left maintaining it.
Another
patch
drops one of the Intel Keem Bay DRM driver maintainers as no longer at the company but there was another co-maintainer listed. Intel had an engineer helping to maintain the Linux kernel's Kprobes code but that too is
no more
with Anil S Keshavamurthy no longer at Intel to oversee the kernel probes code to help with debugging and performance profiling.
Intel also had two engineers working on the T7XX 5G WWAN driver but that too is no more
here
and
here
.
Those are the latest maintainer file patches from Intel today and hopefully the last of it.

data.title: Writing a storage engine for Postgres: An in-memory table access method (2023)
data.author: ibobev
data.article_summary:
Postgres 12引入了可更换存储引擎的功能，类似于MySQL长期支持的特性。尽管目前Postgres的第三方存储引擎开发尚处早期阶段，但像OrioleDB和Citus Columnar等项目正在积极开发中。更换存储引擎有助于根据不同工作负载（如分析型工作负载、写密集型工作负载或内存存储）选择合适的存储方案，同时保留Postgres的其他基础设施优势。

文章还讨论了表访问方法（table access methods）和外部数据包装器（FDWs）的区别，指出表访问方法提供更紧密的集成和更好的性能。作者尝试编写了一个基本的表访问方法原型，并提供了构建和安装自定义Postgres存储引擎的指南和代码示例，代码可在GitHub上找到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：OLTP数据库是否可以采用分层存储系统，特别是内存、NVME缓存和对象存储的组合。

不同观点：
• [支持采用分层存储的观点] rubenvanwyk 提出，OLTP数据库可以采用分层存储系统，将数据保存到内存，缓存到NVME，并最终永久保存到对象存储，每层提供不同的保障级别。这种方法可以提升数据库性能，并且通过分层管理数据，能够根据数据的重要性或访问频率提供不同的存储策略。

• [对现有实践的质疑] o11c 指出，截至2023年，关于这一主题的公开文档非常稀少，唯一的参考资料是PostgreSQL官方文档中非常简略的说明。这暗示了当前可能并没有广泛应用或成熟的解决方案来实现这种分层存储系统，尤其是在OLTP数据库中。

补充讨论：
• [技术实现的挑战] o11c 提供的链接指向PostgreSQL的文档，表明这种分层存储系统的实现可能涉及复杂的底层技术，并且在实际应用中可能缺乏足够的支持和文档。这揭示了在现有数据库系统中实现这种架构可能面临的技术和文档不足的挑战。

44783368.article_content:
With
Postgres 12
,
released in 2019, it became possible to
swap out Postgres's storage
engine
.
This is a feature MySQL has supported for a long time. There are at
least
8 different
built-in
engines you can pick from.
MyRocks
, MySQL on
RocksDB, is another popular third-party distribution.
I assume there will be a renaissance of Postgres storage engines. To
date, the efforts are
nascent.
OrioleDB
and
Citus
Columnar
are two promising third-party table access methods being actively
developed.
Why alternative storage engines?
The ability to swap storage engines is useful because different
workloads sometimes benefit from different storage
approaches. Analytics workloads and columnar storage layouts
go well
together
. Write-heavy
workloads and LSM trees
go well
together
. And
some people like in-memory storage for running integration tests.
By swapping out only the storage engine, you get the benefit of the
rest of the Postgres or MySQL infrastructure. The query language, the
wire protocol, the ecosystem, etc.
Why not foreign data wrappers?
Very little has been written about the difference between foreign data
wrappers (FDWs) and table access methods. Table access methods seems
to be the lower-level layer where presumably you get better
performance and cleaner integration. But there is clearly overlap
between these two extension options.
For example there is a
FDW for
ClickHouse
so when you
create tables and rows and query the tables you are really creating
and querying rows in a ClickHouse server. Similarly there's a
FDW for
RocksDB
. And Citus's columnar
engine works
either
as a foreign data wrapper or a table access method.
The Citus page draws the clearest distinction between FDWs and table
access methods, but even that page is vague. Performance doesn't seem
to be the main difference. Closer integration, and thus the ability to
look more like vanilla Postgres from the outside, seems to be the
gist.
In any case, I wanted to explore the table access method API.
Digging in
I haven't written Postgres extensions before and I've never written C
professionally. If you're familiar with Postgres internals or C and
notice something funky, please
let me know
!
It turns out that almost no one has written how to implement the
minimal table access methods for various storage engine operations. So
after quite a bit of stumbling to get the basics of an in-memory
storage engine working, I'm going to walk you through my approach.
This is prototype-quality code which hopefully will be a useful base
for further exploration.
All code for this post is
available on
GitHub
.
A debug Postgres build
First off, let's make a
debug
build
of
Postgres.
$
git
clone
https
://
github
.
com
/
postgres
/
postgres
$
# An arbitrary commit from `master` after Postgres 16 I am on
$
git
checkout
849172ff4883d44168f96f39d3fde96d0aa34c99
$
cd
postgres
$
.
/
configure
--
enable
-
cassert
--
enable
-
debug
CFLAGS
=
"-ggdb -Og -g3 -fno-omit-frame-pointer"
$
make
-
j8
$
sudo
make
install
This will install Postgres binaries (e.g.
psql
,
pg_ctl
,
initdb
,
pg_config
) into
/usr/local/pgsql/bin
.
I'm going to reference those absolute paths throughout this post
because you might have a system (package manager) install of Postgres
already.
Let's create a database and start up this debug build:
$
/usr/local/pgsql/bin/initdb
test-db
$
/usr/local/pgsql/bin/pg_ctl
-D
test-db
-l
logfile
start
Extension infrastructure
Since we installed Postgres from scratch,
/usr/local/pgsql/bin/pg_config
will supply all of the infrastructure
we need.
The "infrastructure" is basically just
PGXS
:
Postgres Makefile utilities.
It's convention-heavy. So in a new
Makefile
for this project we'll
specify:
MODULES
: Any C sources to build, without the
.c
file extension
EXTENSION
: Extension metadata file, without the
.control
file extension
DATA
: A SQL file that is executed when the extension is loaded, this time with the
.sql
extension
MODULES
=
pgtam
EXTENSION
=
pgtam
DATA
=
pgtam--0.0.1.sql
PG_CONFIG
=
/usr/local/pgsql/bin/pg_config
PGXS
:=
$(
shell
$(
PG_CONFIG
)
--pgxs
)
include $(PGXS)
The final three lines set up the PGXS Makefile library based on the
particular installed Postgres build we want to build the extension
against and install the extension to.
PGXS gives us a few important targets like
make distclean
,
make
,
and
make install
we'll use later on.
pgtam.c
A minimal C file that registers a function capable of serving as a
table access method is:
#include
"postgres.h"
#include
"fmgr.h"
#include
"access/tableam.h"
PG_MODULE_MAGIC
;
const
TableAmRoutine
memam_methods
=
{
.
type
=
T_TableAmRoutine
,
};
PG_FUNCTION_INFO_V1
(
mem_tableam_handler
);
Datum
mem_tableam_handler
(
PG_FUNCTION_ARGS
)
{
PG_RETURN_POINTER
(
&
memam_methods
);
}
If you want to read about extension basics without the complexity of
table access methods, you can find a complete, minimal Postgres
extension I wrote to validate the
infrastructure
here
. Or
you can follow a
larger
tutorial
.

data.author: olieidel
data.article_summary:
文章讨论了德国退出税对企业主的影响，特别是对计划移居国外的企业家。退出税适用于拥有超过1%股份的企业主，包括外国公司。税额通过过去三年平均收益乘以13.75，再乘以60%，然后按个人所得税率（通常为42%）计算，简化公式为：平均收益 × 3.5。

文章将德国人分为四类：
1. **雇员**：不受退出税影响。
2. **亏损企业主**：企业价值为零或接近零，退出税影响小（但有投资的初创企业可能受影响）。
3. **盈利企业主**：受影响最大，可能面临高额退出税。例如，年收益€200k的企业主可能面临€700k的退出税。
4. **大企业主**：可通过税务顾问设立信托基金避税。

文章强调，盈利但不非常大的企业主（如年收益€200k）受退出税影响最严重，因为他们的企业价值较高，但可能没有足够资金支付高额税款。文章呼吁关注这一问题，认为这是对德国企业家的一种束缚。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：德国退出税（exit tax）政策及其合理性、操作复杂性和对企业及个人的影响

不同观点：
• **支持退出税政策**：部分评论认为退出税在资本利得税和所得税的征收方式上存在根本差异，政策的初衷是合理的。例如，[derriz]指出资本利得通常具有非流动性和估值困难的特点，因此推迟征税是合理的，政策能防止通过移居避税国家来逃避税收。

• **政策存在缺陷和操作复杂性**：[nolverostae]指出，尽管可以通过将公司股份放入德国内的控股公司来规避部分税收，但仍需聘请昂贵的税务顾问，且估值方法可能不合理，特别是当无法提供符合德国标准的估值时，税务机关会基于收益进行假设估值。

• **对创业者和企业不友好**：[geff82]和[zwnow]提到，自2022年起，企业主甚至无法将公司迁往其他欧盟国家，这严重限制了自由流动，且德国繁琐的官僚程序和严格的劳工权利对创业并不友好。

• **国际对比与法律挑战**：[profstasiak]质疑美国公民移居欧盟后需支付双重税，[garyclarke27]则认为欧盟的自由流动原则可能受到退出税政策的挑战，可能值得法律挑战。[chaosprint]提到挪威的退出税和财富税也存在类似问题，尤其对风险投资驱动的科技初创企业不利。

• **规避策略**：一些评论讨论了规避退出税的潜在策略。例如，[merek]提出通过在目标国家成立新公司，转移用户和收入，最终将德国公司清算。而[elephant81]建议通过离岸许可协议，将大部分收入转移至爱尔兰公司，减少德国公司的利润。

补充讨论：
• **税务顾问的角色**：[weinzierl]对设立信托等复杂税务规划的难度提出疑问，指出如果净资产超过一定数额，聘请专业税务顾问可以简化操作。

• **争议焦点**：政策的估值方法和“流动性挤压”问题被认为是主要争议点，特别是当税务机关基于收益假设估值时，可能导致不合理的结果。[eqvinox]质疑某些评论中提到的具体数字和规则的准确性，呼吁提供法律依据。

总结：讨论围绕德国退出税的合理性、实际操作中的复杂性及其对个人和企业的不同影响展开，同时涉及规避策略和国际税法对比。

Exit Tax: Leave Germany Before Your Business Gets Big
Aug 7, 2025
•
Startups
•
7 min read
Here’s an interesting take on Germany’s exit tax, which I have
written about
before:
Leave Germany before your business gets big.
What do I mean by that?
I mean that once you’re a business owner in Germany and your business has reached a certain size, you are essentially barred from ever moving out of the country again.
Crazy, right? I think it’s also pretty crazy that no one really talks about this. This is, quite literally, erecting a “Berlin Wall” around German entrepreneurs, forcing them to stay in the country.
Germany’s Exit Tax
But first things first. What is Germany’s exit tax?
In simple terms, you’re hit by Germany’s exit tax once you hold more than 1% in any limited liability company (foreign companies included!). So if you own 100% of a German GmbH, you’re hit by exit tax. But also if you e.g. own 2% of a US company.
And then your exit tax is calculated by taking the average of the past 3 years of earnings of that company, multiplied by 13.75 (which is crazy), and then taking 60% of that which is taxed at your personal income tax rate (likely 42%; Teileinkünfteverfahren). So:
(Average earnings of past 3 years) * 13.75 * 0.6 * 0.42
Simplified: (Average earnings of past 3 years) * ~3.5
I’ve simplified the formula for you a bit: It boils down to multiplying the average earnings with ~3.5.
With this calculation in hand, we can do surprisingly interesting things.
We can segment German people into four distinct groups, with greatly varying barriers of ever leaving the country:
Some People Can Leave Germany, Others Can’t
Employees:
The simplest case – no shares in any companies. They can just leave the country and are not hit by any exit tax. People say Germany is a good country for being an employee, and this is also true for exit tax.
Business owners of unprofitable companies:
Still a reasonably simple case – these people have shares in a business, but its value is calculated as zero, so while they are hit by exit tax, the sum might be zero (caveat: see notes on startups below)
Business owners of profitable companies:
The ugliest case – people who own shares in a business which is profitable. Its value, in the eyes of the financial authorities, is likely high, given the factor of 13.75. These people will be hit by significant exit tax; they usually don’t have a crazy amount of savings, and don’t have the resources to engage fancy tax advisors.
Business owners of huge companies:
You might think this is worse, but it’s actually not. As soon as your net worth goes beyond ~€2m, you can afford fancy tax advisors which set up a trust in Liechtenstein for you (yes seriously) which allow you to dodge the exit tax. So this group is simpler, for exit tax purposes.
(Note on startups (group 2): If your startup raised investment, the financial authorities might take that last investment-round valuation as actual valuation, even if your company is not profitable. So that puts you into group 3 instead as you will be hit by significant exit tax.)
So, what I’d like to talk about is group 3: Business owners of profitable companies. And let’s zoom in even further, because all businesses start out small.
Let’s look at scenario 3a:
You’re a business owner of a profitable business, but it’s not hugely profitable. It might have, say, 50k€ earnings per year (nice job), but you haven’t been paying yourself a salary yet. Instead of taking the 13.75 multiple of the financial authorities you could now task someone with assessing the value of your business (which is a viable strategy, by the way), and they would come up with a result that your “real” business earnings are zero or negative, because the market rate for a CEO would be €100k – €120k / year, and if you’d be paying that to yourself, your business earnings would go below zero.
So, you can realistically assume that your business valuation, in the eyes of the financial authorities, is actually zero, and your exit tax amount will be zero, too.
Okay. But let’s fast-forward a few years and look at the same business again. Maybe it’s still a small business, but now it’s doing slightly better:
Scenario 3b:
You’re a business owner of a profitable business which is decently profitable. It has €200k earnings per year
and
you’re paying yourself a market-rate salary of €120k / year. This now hits you with a brutal exit tax burden because there’s no trivial way of arguing that the value of your business is low. Using our formula above, the exit tax you’re looking at is ~€700k (€200k * 3.5). Crazy!

Scenario 3a
Scenario 3b
Earnings / year
€50k
€200k
Your CEO salary / year
€0
€120k
Potential exit tax
€0
€700k
And this is crazy! How crazy? People might point at the business owner of scenario 3b and say “but yeah, €700k exit tax is fine, he owns a hugely profitable business”. But no, it’s

data.title: Show HN: Stasher – Burn-after-read secrets from the CLI, no server, no trust
data.author: stasher-dev
data.article_summary: Stasher CLI 是一个命令行工具，用于安全地共享一次性秘密信息。它通过本地使用 AES-256-GCM 加密，后端仅存储密文而不保存密钥。秘密信息设置10分钟的有效期，并采用 "读后即焚" 机制，确保只能访问一次。使用方法包括通过 `npx` 命令创建、检索和删除秘密信息。该工具无需登录，强调零信任和端到端加密。当前版本为 v1.4.0，未来计划增加对 AAD 的支持。项目主要使用 TypeScript 开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某密码分享工具的安全性、实用性及其实现方式的讨论

不同观点：
• [支持实用性但质疑实现方式] coldstartops认为该工具将一个两步的密码分享过程合并为一步，但引入了服务器风险。他质疑为何不使用Signal或Telegram等其他更简单的安全渠道来分享加密密码。
• [对AI生成代码和匿名作者的担忧] cmeacham98和Disposal8433对该工具的代码由AI生成以及作者匿名表示严重担忧，认为这在安全敏感软件中是重大隐患，建议谨慎使用。
• [对服务器必要性的质疑] scosman和h43z对服务器的存在提出疑问，认为从逻辑上来说，密码不触及服务器也可以实现相同的安全性。
• [推荐替代工具] indigodaddy推荐使用Password Pusher作为替代工具，认为其易于部署且功能合理。
• [对客户端安全的关注] pastage希望能在浏览器中运行代码，以确保客户端生成密钥时不进行网络连接。

补充讨论：
• [对CLI安全性的批评] pxc指出不应通过命令行传递秘密，因为这会留下shell历史记录，且容易被进程检查获取。同时批评工具的“供应链安全”和设计语言不一致。
• [对GPG的推荐] i_am_proteus和precompute推荐使用GPG，认为其更安全可靠，并建议非技术人员使用Signal或简单加密方法如ROT13。
• [对命令行历史记录的建议] jiji指出命令行输出可能被记录在.bash_history中，建议在执行命令前进行适当配置。
• [幽默回应] Thatdudeyouknow以幽默方式回应，未提供实质性意见。

争议焦点：
• 该工具是否通过引入服务器增加了不必要的风险，以及代码由AI生成和作者匿名是否严重影响工具的可信度和安全性。

data.title: Partially Matching Zig Enums
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一种在Zig语言中处理枚举部分匹配的技巧。通常，处理枚举时需要为每个变体编写单独的处理代码，但有时多个变体需要共享一些处理逻辑。简单的做法可能导致代码重复，而重构枚举又可能不适合所有使用场景。文章首先展示了一种通过运行时恐慌（runtime panic）来解决共享逻辑的方案，但这并不理想。随后，文章提出了一种利用Zig的编译时特性（`comptime`）和内联开关（`inline switch`）的更优雅且编译器验证的解决方案。这种方法通过使用`comptime unreachable`确保在编译时检查不可达分支，从而避免运行时错误。文章最后展示了错误引入如何导致编译失败，以证明该方法的健壮性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Zig语言的创新特性，尤其是编译时元编程和comptime特性。

不同观点：
• judofyr认为Zig在编译时元编程和`comptime`特性上有显著创新，不能简单地因为Zig是内存不安全语言就忽视它。他特别提到`inline else`和`comptime`等特性，认为这些特性能够有效减少运行时开销，并且希望其他语言也能借鉴这些想法。

• uecker对Zig的这些新特性持一种调侃态度，认为这些特性在C语言中早已存在，只是其他语言现在才开始关注和引入类似的编译时元编程功能。

• loeg指出Zig的`comptime unreachable`特性相较于C++中的`__builtin_unreachable()`更具优势，因为后者缺乏对不可达位置的验证，而仅仅依赖优化器处理。loeg通常推荐在运行时使用`assert`等方法来处理不可达代码。

• agons对Zig编译器的类型缩减能力提出疑问，询问为什么在`U::A(_) | U::B(_)`这样的保护模式下不能直接缩减类型`u`，从而不需要借助博客中提到的解决方案。这显示出对Zig类型系统的理解存在不确定性。

• spiffyk赞赏Zig的`comptime`特性，认为它不仅可以用于预计算，还能用于编译时错误检查。他承认自己在使用时常常忽略后一种用途，但认为这其实非常有价值。

• rvrb对Zig中可以内联`else`以外的分支表示惊喜，认为这是一个非常酷的用法。

• the__alchemist幽默地指出文章开头对数据结构术语混乱的承认，显示出对术语不一致问题的关注。

• veber-alex质疑这些特性是否仅在编译时已知值的情况下才有用，暗示对Zig特性的实际应用场景存在疑虑。

• dlahoda提供了一个Rust代码示例，指出类似的功能在Rust中会导致编译失败，暗示Rust在处理这类特性上的不同。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点之一是Zig的创新性。judofyr和uecker对Zig的创新程度有不同看法，前者认为Zig在元编程上有显著创新，而后者认为这些特性早已存在。
• 另一个讨论点是Zig编译器的类型缩减能力，agons对此提出疑问，显示出对Zig类型系统理解的不确定性。
• 不同的评论者对Zig特性的实用性和应用场景有不同看法，veber-alex和spiffyk分别对编译时已知值的必要性和`comptime`特性的价值提出不同见解。

通过这些讨论，可以看出Zig语言在编译时元编程和类型系统上的特性引发了不同开发者的关注和讨论，有些特性被认为是创新且有价值的，而有些则被认为早已有之或实用性有限。

44845017.article_content:
Partially Matching Zig Enums
Aug 8, 2025
A short post about a neat little Zig idiom. Consider your average {sum
type, variant, tagged union, enum, alt}:
enum
U
{
A
(
i32
),
B
(
i32
),
C,
}
Usually, you handle it like this:
match
u {
U::
A
(_) =>
handle_a
(),
U::
B
(_) =>
handle_b
(),
U::C =>
handle_c
(),
}
But once in a while, there’s common handling code you want to run for
several variants. The most straightforward way is to duplicate:
match
u {
U::
A
(_) => {
handle_ab
();
handle_a
();
}
U::
B
(_) => {
handle_ab
();
handle_b
();
}
U::C =>
handle_c
(),
}
But this gets awkward if common parts are not easily extractable into
function. The “proper” way to do this is to refactor the enum:
enum
U
{
AB
(AB),
C
}
enum
AB
{
A
(
i32
),
B
(
i32
),
}
This gets
very
awkward if there’s one hundred usages of
U
, 95 of them look better with flat structure, one needs
common code for ab case, and the four remaining need common code for
ac.
The universal recipe for solving the AB problem relies on a runtime
panic:
match
u {
U::
A
(_) | U::
B
(_) => {
handle_ab
();
match
u {
U::
A
(_) =>
handle_a
(),
U::
B
(_) =>
handle_b
(),
_ =>
unreachable!
(),
}
}
U::C =>
handle_c
(),
}
And… this is fine, really! I wrote code of this shape many times, and
it never failed at runtime due to a misapplied refactor later. Still,
every time I write that
unreachable
, I die inside a
little. Surely there should be some way to explain to the compiler
that
c
is really unreachable there? Well, as I realized
an hour ago, in Zig, you can!
This is the awkward runtime-panicky and theoretically brittle version:
switch
(u) {
.a, .b =>
|
_, ab
|
{
handle_ab();
switch
(ab) {
.a => handle_a(),
.b => handle_b(),
else
=>
unreachable
,
}
},
.c => handle_c(),
}
And here’s a bullet-proof compiler-checked one:
const
U =
union
(
enum
) {
a:
i32
,
b:
i32
,
c,
};
fn
handle
(u: U)
void
{
switch
(u) {
inline
.a, .b =>
|
_, ab
|
{
handle_ab();
switch
(ab) {
.a => handle_a(),
.b => handle_b(),
else
=>
comptime
unreachable
,
}
},
.c => handle_c(),
}
}
fn
handle_ab
()
void
{}
fn
handle_a
()
void
{}
fn
handle_b
()
void
{}
fn
handle_c
()
void
{}
pub
fn
main
()
void
{ handle(.c); }
There are two tricks here.
inline .a, .b
forces the
compiler to generate the program twice, where
ab
is bound to
comptime
value. The second trick is
comptime unreachable
, which instructs the compiler to fail if
it gets to the else branch. But, because
ab
is known at
comptime, compiler knows that
else
is in fact
unreachable, and doesn’t hit the error.
Adding a bug fails compilation, as intended:
switch
(u) {
inline
.a, .b, .c =>
|
_, ab
|
{
handle_ab();
switch
(ab) {
.a => handle_a(),
.b => handle_b(),
else
=>
comptime
unreachable
,
}
},
}
$
./zig/zig build-exe partial-match.zig
partial-match.zig:14:34: error: reached unreachable code
else => comptime unreachable,
^~~~~~~~~~~

data.title: Why Wisconsin's county highways are lettered, not numbered (2019)
data.author: kaladin-jasnah
data.article_summary: 在威斯康星州，县级公路使用字母而非数字命名，以区别于州级公路，避免维护和修理工作的重复。这一系统自1917年开始实施，由各县自行命名，由于字母只有26个，常出现重复，单字母用完后会使用双字母或多字母组合。威斯康星州是全美首个区分州县公路的州，并率先举办道路学校，分享最佳实践和创新，保持在交通领域的领先地位。该系统由威斯康星县级公路协会管理，该协会对此历史感到自豪。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对各州和县道路命名系统的不同观点及其实际影响

不同观点：
• [ehaskins] 认为Google Maps应该学会正确发音县道路的名称，而不是简单地将其读作"County Road North"。这相比人工智能（AGI）的实现应该更容易。

• [bombcar] 指出Siri会错误地将县道路称为高速公路，并提到自己正在寻找County Road PP，打算亲自开车去验证，并让孩子嘲笑Siri的错误。

• [abecode] 分享个人经验，提到County Road AF是一个他喜欢的地方，靠近Fall Creek和Augusta。

• [jethkl] 引用Conway's Law来解释州和县道路系统的分离是为了避免维护和修理队伍重复工作，并提供了一个维基百科链接以支持其论点。

• [brettgriffin] 对使用字母来区分县道路的必要性提出质疑，认为即使在没有计算机和互联网的时代，也应该有可能设计出一个跨72个县不冲突的数字系统。

44802484.article_content:
If you’ve taken a drive on one of Wisconsin’s iconic scenic roads, chances are you’ve noticed a bit of alphabet soup.
Signs with names like BB, CV, N and SS flank Wisconsin’s county roads, and Shelly from Marshall wanted to know why.
She asked: “Why are Wisconsin’s county roads labeled with letters instead of numbers?”
Stay connected to Wisconsin news — your way
Get trustworthy reporting and unique local stories from WPR delivered directly to your inbox.
Email
Name
This field is for validation purposes and should be left unchanged.
So WPR’s
WHYsconsin
reached out to Daniel Fedderly, executive director of the Wisconsin County Highway Association — a nonprofit organization that represents the state’s 72 county highway and public works departments — to find out.
Jasonic
(CC BY-NC-ND)
“It’s good to start off with a little background,” Fedderly said. “We have state highways that are under state jurisdiction … then we have county highways that are under each of the individual counties — 72 counties in the state — and those county highways are under the individual county’s jurisdiction.”
From a practical perspective, Fedderly explained it was necessary to keep the two systems separate so that maintenance and repairs wouldn’t be duplicated.
“They needed to be able to keep them separate, and hence, they separated them by the numbers and letters,” he said. “That way they could keep track of whose was whose because you had the same people, the same crews, the same individuals taking care of several different sections of road.”
It’s a system that’s been in place for more than 100 years, Fedderly said.
“That system was first set up in 1917. And the Wisconsin County Highway Association was initially formed in 1911,” he said. “It is credited as being the oldest such association in the nation and the Wisconsin Legislature saw fit to form the County Highway Association, so that there was a methodology for how they coordinated their efforts in terms of taking care of the state system.”
Naming each highway is up to the individual county, Fedderly said.
“The ultimate decision for naming is left with the county board, largely through the highway commissioner, to the highway committee, to the county board,” he said. “The county board is the one that designates what a new highway may be.”
And because there are only 26 letters in the alphabet, you see a lot of duplicates, he said.
“You’ll find in virtually every county, certain letters that are, I guess, for lack of a better term, the more popular. … I can’t say every county has a county trunk highway B, for example, or a county highway N for example, but you will find that the vast majority of the counties will have the same ones because we only have the 26 letters to work with,” Fedderly said.
Fedderly also noted that double letters and a combination of two or more letters is a common practice when all the single letters are already in use.
“As you can imagine, over the last 100-plus years, as the county gained more roads and took over certain roads and things of that nature, they used up all the letters of the alphabet. And so subsequently then once they’ve used them up, they would go to the double TT, double S, things of that nature. And then after that they would start doing variations there, you know, County CE or something of that nature,” he said.
Jimmy Emerson, DVM
(CC BY-NC-ND)
In addition to being the first state to differentiate its state and county roads, Wisconsin was also the first state in the nation to host road schools.
“We would bring in the commissioners, committee members, contractors, all the folks that perform maintenance and construction of our roadways, and we’d share best practices, share the newest innovations, new ways to do things, share information to make sure that we’re getting the best return on our investment in Wisconsin,” he said. “Today Wisconsin is still recognized as the leader. We do two road schools a year for our transportation stakeholders and continue to be a leader in terms of innovative efforts and getting the best return we can for the money.”
It’s something Fedderly and the Association is proud of.
“We at the Wisconsin County Highway Association are proud of that history because we’ve been a leader in the nation for forever in terms of formation,” Fedderly said.

and we might answer it in a future

data.title: I prefer human-readable file formats
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 这篇文章提到，为了区分人类和机器人，系统将设置一个虚拟的Cookie。人类用户可以处理这个Cookie，而机器人通常无法管理Cookie。通过这种方式，系统能够有效辨别用户是否为真人，从而提高安全性或防止自动程序的滥用。这个方法常用于防止恶意爬虫或自动脚本访问网站。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文件格式的可读性与效率之间的权衡，包括文本格式与二进制格式的优劣对比。

不同观点：
• **支持文本格式**：
  - **[bregma]**：基于文本的格式（如GNU Cash和Plain-Text Accounting）允许信息灵活备份和转换，专注于内容而非工具或格式。经过四十多年的经验，仍偏好人类可读的文件格式。
  - **[whobre]**：只要工具支持，人类可读格式（如编辑器或查看器）就可以很方便。即使是二进制文件，如果有工具支持，也没有问题。
  - **[mschwaig]**：Categorical Configuration Language (CCL) 利用有意义的空白字符，避免了在多行字符串中转义，尽管某些内容未完全指定。

• **支持二进制格式**：
  - **[mriet]**：在生物信息学领域，文本格式在面对超大文件（1-2Mb到1Tb）时效率极低，处理时间过长，可读性没有实际价值。
  - **[refactor_master]**：二进制格式在存储空间和处理速度上更有效率，尤其是在1985年那样的计算资源受限时代。
  - **[kamatour]**：可读文件在面对超大文件（如1TB）时会变得难以处理。

• **中立或混合观点**：
  - **[mxmlnkn]**：虽然同意文本格式在小文件（如配置文件）中的优点，但对大文件（如1GB+ JSON文件）效率低下。流式处理和SIMD解析不能同时实现，且JSONL格式需要额外支持。
  - **[kjellsbells]**：每种文件格式在阅读、理解、操作、短期和长期检索方面各有优劣。文本文件并不总是高效或易读的，特别是在处理超大文件或二进制数据时。
  - **[nine_k]**：二进制格式在有适当渲染器时也是可读的，ASCII/UTF-8文本格式无需特殊处理即可阅读。
  - **[Too]**：寻找一种既高效又可访问的格式，如Parquet、Protobuf或SQLite，但这些格式在编辑和diff工具支持上不如文本格式。

补充讨论：
• **CSV和其他文本格式的缺陷**：
  - **[IanCal]**：CSV文件在编辑时容易出错，缺乏基本的检查和验证，隐藏的含义需要外部文档说明。
  - **[graphviz]**：引用了一项关于CSV文件解析的研究，指出许多潜在的陷阱，并提到工具（如Miller）对文本表格处理的重要性。

• **二进制格式的可读性与工具支持**：
  - **[adregan]**：是否有包含格式说明的二进制格式？这可能提高二进制格式的可访问性。

争议焦点：
• **文本格式与二进制格式在超大文件处理上的效率和可操作性**。
• **CSV等文本格式在编辑和解析过程中的易错性和缺乏验证机制**。

data.author: Bogdanp

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：[关于6NF（第六范式）在数据库设计中的实用性和理论价值]

不同观点：
• [支持6NF的理论价值]
  - Joker_vD认为6NF被误解为“不实用”是因为大多数数据库从业者错误地认为数据模型中的每个关系应该直接对应一个表/B树结构
  - 强调关系模型的核心是抽象存储实现细节，专注于查询的概念性API
  - 暗示6NF的"荒谬"印象源于对关系模型基本原理的误解

• [强调SQL实践应用]
  - gnat推崇注重实际应用的SQL写作方式
  - 赞赏能将理论清晰应用于实践而不过度纠缠于数据库理论术语的写作风格
  - 暗示过于理论化的讨论可能影响SQL的实际使用价值

• [关于6NF具体实施的讨论]
  - reactordev针对6NF具体实现提出技术性建议：
    - 指出真正的6NF不需要依赖列顺序，而是需要明确的命名约定
    - 提供具体命名示例（id, manager_id等）
    - 建议将相关属性组分离为链接表以进一步规范化数据
    - 指出即使是经验丰富的开发者也常混淆属性和链接的概念

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于数据库理论（特别是高级范式如6NF）与实际应用之间的平衡
• Joker_vD与reactordev的讨论形成了理论原则与具体实现方法之间的对话
• gnat的观点引入了对理论讨论实用价值的质疑，形成了第三方视角

data.title: What's wrong with the JSON gem API?
data.author: ezekg
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Ruby的JSON gem中API的设计问题和过时（deprecation）处理，特别是`JSON.load`和`JSON.parse`的区别，以及`create_additions: true`选项带来的安全风险。作者成为gem维护者的主要原因不是性能问题，而是改进设计不佳和危险的API。`create_additions: true`选项允许通过`json_class`自动实例化对象，可能导致安全漏洞，类似YAML中的问题。为了解决这一问题，作者已将隐式的`create_additions: true`标记为过时，并引入`JSON.unsafe_load`作为替代。此外，文章还介绍了如何在Ruby中处理过时警告，建议在测试套件中启用过时警告以提前发现潜在问题。作者还提到可以使用`deprecation_toolkit` gem来管理大型项目中的过时问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JSON处理中的不同技术问题，包括重复键的行为、JSON库的使用以及解析选项的命名和默认行为。

不同观点：
• [kazinator的观点]  
  - 认为JSON中重复键的行为是“未指定行为”，标准没有明确规定如何处理。
  - 生成带有重复键的JSON的软件会导致下游处理器出现未定义行为，因此可以视为输出有问题。
  - 强调如果生成的JSON包含重复键，生成者应对因此引发的任何问题负责。

• [nurettin的观点]  
  - 对“json gem”的概念有疑问，指出JSON库是随Ruby附带的，而不是通过`gem install`命令安装的。
  - 分享了自己使用`require 'json/ext'`的经验，指出C扩展版本更快。

• [ezekg的观点]  
  - 建议将JSON解析中的`:symbolize_names`关键字重命名为`:symbolize_keys`，因为前者容易让人困惑。

• [jmull的观点]  
  - 认为改变处理重复键的默认行为是不必要的。
  - 强烈反对故意引入随机bug到依赖该库的应用程序中。

补充讨论：
